items.title: Foreigners accused of visa overstay can't be kept in detention centres after getting bail: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that foreign nationals accused of overstaying their visas cannot be directed to remain in detention centres as a condition for being granted bail. A Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj said that imposing such a condition would defeat the very purpose of granting bail. It added that foreign nationals accused of violating immigration laws are entitled to be considered for bail in the same manner as other criminal accused. “A direction imposing a condition wherein the foreign national is restricted to a detention centre would frustrate the very order of bail and hence, cannot be imposed. Such a power can be exercised by the Central Government by an order under Section 3(2)(g) of the 1946 Act [Foreigners Act], or under Paragraph 8 of the Immigration and Foreigners Order, 2025,” the Court said. However, it clarified that granting bail does not legalise a foreign national's continued stay in India or operate as a substitute for a valid visa. items.title: What a new Pew study says about India’s Hindu and Muslim populations
items.summary: Between 2020 and 2070, India’s total population is projected to expand from 1.40 billion to 1.70 billion, in which Hindus will remain the overwhelming majority while Muslims represent the fastest-growing religion. A new Pew Research Center study titled ‘The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2020-2070’ released on Wednesday, November 18 estimates that the population share of Hindus in India will decrease from about 79% in 2020 to about 76% in 2070, while the Muslim share will increase from about 15% to 20%. Despite this dip, Hindus will maintain their numerical dominance, continuing to comprise more than three-quarters of the nation’s populace. India’s Hindu population is expected to rise from 1.113 billion to 1.289 billion while the Muslim population will grow from 213 million to nearly 334 million. The changes stem mainly from differences in age and fertility, the study says. The fertility rate for Indian Hindus was estimated at 1.9 children per woman in the 2020–2025 period, while it is 2.3 for per woman for Muslims.
